context: Tests whether the agent follows contract-first OpenAPI 3.1 design, enforces Bearer JWT authentication with correct error codes, restricts uploads to jpg/jpeg/png/pdf using Content-Type detection, and applies the exact 10 MiB size ceiling with the correct error status.

checklist.name: OpenAPI spec file present
checklist.description: A file named openapi.yaml or openapi.json exists in the working directory

checklist.name: OpenAPI version 3.1
checklist.description: The spec file declares openapi version 3.1.x (not 3.0.x or 2.x)

checklist.name: Bearer token auth declared
checklist.description: The upload endpoint requires a Bearer token (JWT) as documented in the spec — e.g. a securityScheme of type http with scheme bearer

checklist.name: 401 for invalid auth
checklist.description: The implementation returns HTTP 401 when the Authorization header is missing, malformed, or contains an expired/invalid token

checklist.name: File type allowlist
checklist.description: Only jpg, jpeg, png, and pdf file types are accepted; all other types are rejected

checklist.name: Content-Type based validation
checklist.description: File type validation inspects the Content-Type (MIME type) of the uploaded file rather than relying solely on the file extension

checklist.name: 415 for rejected type
checklist.description: The implementation returns HTTP 415 when an upload is rejected due to an unsupported file type

checklist.name: 10 MiB size limit
checklist.description: The maximum accepted file size is exactly 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes) — not a different value such as 10 MB (10,000,000 bytes) or another approximation

checklist.name: 413 for oversized file
checklist.description: The implementation returns HTTP 413 when an upload exceeds the size limit

checklist.name: Spec-implementation alignment
checklist.description: The HTTP status codes and authentication scheme defined in openapi.yaml (or openapi.json) match those used in the implementation source code
